UPSC Section Officers' LDCE 2026 Examination Centres

The Combined Section Officers' (Grade-'B') LDCE, 2026 will be held at the following five centres. 

S.No. Centre
1 Chennai
2 Delhi
3 Kolkata
4 Mumbai
5 Nagpur

No request for change of examination centre will be entertained. If a candidate appears at a venue other than the one indicated in the e-Admit Card, they will not be allowed to take the examination. Centres and dates are liable to change at the discretion of the Commission.

UPSC Section Officers and Stenographers LDCE Application Fee 2026

Application fee details are not specified in the provided notification excerpts for either examination. Candidates should check the Examination Specific Module on the online application portal (https://upsconline.nic.in) or the full official notification on https://upsc.gov.in for applicable fee information, including any fee payment steps that the helpdesk can assist with during the application window.

UPSC Section Officers' LDCE 2026 Exam Pattern

The Combined Section Officers' (Grade-'B') LDCE, 2026 includes Objective Type Question Papers as well as descriptive papers. The notification specifically references the following papers for tie-breaking purposes:

  • Paper-II: Procedure of Practice in the Govt. of India Secretariat and attached Offices and General Financial and Service Rules (duly taking into account the requirement of relevant categories of services)
  • Paper-III: Noting and Drafting, Precis Writing

There will be a penalty (negative marking) for wrong answers marked in the Objective Type Question Papers; the specific quantum of negative marking is not stated in the provided excerpt. Marks obtained by candidates will be rounded off up to two decimal digits at all stages of the examination, using the standard rounding-off principle, wherever applicable. Detailed exam pattern and syllabus for the Stenographers' LDCE are not specified in the provided notification excerpt.

Also Read: UPSC ESE Notification 2027 Out - Apply Online for 480 Engineering Services Examination Vacancies

UPSC Section Officers and Stenographers LDCE Selection Process 2026

For the Section Officers' Grade-B LDCE, admission to the Written Examination and evaluation of Service Record is purely provisional, subject to candidates satisfying the prescribed eligibility conditions. If it is found, on verification before or after the Written Examination or evaluation of Service Records, that a candidate does not fulfil any eligibility condition, their candidature will be cancelled by the Commission.

UPSC Section Officers' LDCE Tie-Breaking Principles

Where candidates' Final Marks (aggregate) are equal, ties will be resolved in the following order:

  1. The candidate securing more marks in the written total will be ranked higher.
  2. If still equal, the candidate securing more marks in Paper-II and Paper-III put together will be ranked higher.
  3. If still equal, the candidate securing more marks in Paper-III (Noting & Drafting, Precis Writing) will be ranked higher.
  4. If still equal, the candidate senior in age will be ranked higher.
  5. If a tie still persists, it will be resolved at the discretion of the Commission.

UPSC Section Officers' LDCE Representation on Question Papers & Answer Keys

Candidates who appear in the examination will get an opportunity to submit representations on the questions asked and on the Provisional Answer Keys of the Objective Type Question Paper(s), within a window of five days — from the 3rd day of the examination date to 06:00 PM of the 7th day. Representations must be submitted online via the Commission's website under "Examinations > Representations on Question Paper & Provisional Answer Keys"; representations by email, post, hand, or any other mode will not be accepted, and none will be accepted after the five-day window closes.

UPSC Section Officers' LDCE Face Authentication and Venue Rules

  • All candidates must undergo mandatory face authentication at the examination venue.
  • Entry into the examination venue closes 30 minutes prior to commencement of the examination in each session; no entry is allowed after closure under any circumstance.
  • Use of mobile phones (even switched off), pagers, electronic equipment, programmable devices, storage media, smart watches, AI-enabled glasses, cameras, or Bluetooth devices capable of communication is strictly prohibited; violation may lead to disciplinary action, including a ban from future examinations.
  • Candidates are advised not to bring valuable or costly items to the venue, as no safe-keeping arrangement will be made; the Commission will not be responsible for any loss.

How to Apply for UPSC Section Officers and Stenographers LDCE 2026

UPSC LDCE Apply Online process uses the Commission's common Online Application Portal, which applies to both the Section Officers' and Stenographers' examinations.

  1. Visit the Commission's online application portal: https://upsconline.nic.in.
  2. Complete Account Creation, Universal Registration, and the Common Application Form (CAF) — these three modules are common to all UPSC examination applications and can be filled anytime. A Universal Registration Number (URN) is generated on registration, common for all Commission examinations for the candidate's lifetime.
  3. Fill the fourth module — the Examination Specific Form — for the Combined Section Officers' (Grade-'B') LDCE, 2026 and/or the Combined Stenographers' (Grade-'B'/Grade-'I') LDCE, during the application window (16.09.2026 to 06.10.2026). This generates an Application Number specific to that examination.
  4. Upload your photograph and also capture a live photograph while filling the CAF, ensuring both are clear as per the instructions on "Instructions and FAQs > Instruction for filling the form > Photos and Signature".
  5. Sign three times (one below the other) on a plain white paper using black ink, and upload the scanned signature; it must be clear and legible.
  6. Submit the requisite information and supporting documents for claims such as date of birth and educational qualification, along with the URN, CAF, and Examination Specific Module (including fee and centre selection); failure to provide required information/documents will result in cancellation of candidature.
  7. (For Section Officers' LDCE) Take a printout of the completed online application by 06.10.2026, and submit the complete printed copy to your respective Ministry/Department for verification/certification. Your Ministry/Department will forward it to the concerned Cadre Controlling Authority (CCA), with a copy endorsed to the Commission, so that it reaches UPSC by the prescribed date of 23.10.2026, addressed to the Under Secretary (E-VI), Union Public Service Commission, Dholpur House, Shahjahan Road, New Delhi–110069.
  8. Download the e-Admit Card from the Commission's website once issued, on the last working day of the week preceding the examination date; no admit card will be sent by post.

Applicants are strongly advised to use their Aadhaar Card as an ID document for easy, effortless, and seamless verification and authentication of ID and other details.

UPSC Section Officers and Stenographers LDCE 2026 – Important Instructions

  • Candidates should carefully refer to the Notice and Rules before filling the application to confirm eligibility; prescribed conditions cannot be relaxed.
  • Candidates must finally select their preferred examination centre before submitting the application (Section Officers' LDCE); no request for change of centre will be entertained under any circumstances.
  • Admission to the examination at all stages is purely provisional, subject to satisfying prescribed eligibility conditions; candidature will be cancelled if found ineligible at any stage.
  • Candidates must produce their official Identity Card at the time of the examination, along with the e-Admit Card.
  • Signatures on the application form, Attendance List, and correspondence with the Commission must be identical; any variation may lead to cancellation of candidature.
  • No correspondence will be entertained to change any entries made in the application form after submission, as forms are processed by a computerized system.
  • Candidates are not entitled to any Travelling Allowance from the Commission for attending the examination.
  • Only candidates whose printed copy of the online application is forwarded by the concerned CCA (for the Section Officers' LDCE) will be considered for admission to the examination; the Commission is not responsible for non-receipt or delay in receipt of applications, and late applications will be summarily rejected.
  • Applicants must provide a valid and active email ID while creating their account, as the Commission may use electronic mode to contact candidates.
  • A one-time facility is available to update/modify the URN Profile; changes will apply only to applications submitted after the URN Profile is re-locked, not to applications already submitted.
  • All communications regarding an application should be addressed to the Under Secretary (E.VI), UPSC, Dholpur House, Shahjahan Road, New Delhi-110069, and must include: name and year of examination, URN, Application Number, Roll Number (if received), full name in block letters, complete postal address, and valid registered email ID and mobile number. Communications lacking these particulars may not be attended to.

HCL FTE Recruitment 2026 Eligibility Criteria

HCL FTE Recruitment 2026 Selection Process

Selection is based entirely on performance in the Personal Interview (PI) – 100% weightage. There is no written exam by default, though HCL reserves the right to conduct a written screening test to shortlist candidates for the interview, if required.

Zone of Consideration & Shortlisting

  • Candidates are called for interview in the ratio of 1:5 (5 candidates per advertised vacancy); for a single vacancy, 10 candidates are shortlisted.
  • If fewer than 5 applications are received for a post, the Selection Committee will assess and state the suitability of the interviewed candidates directly.
  • Further shortlisting may be done from the eligible pool if posts remain vacant due to low turnout or an exhausted waitlist.
  • Shortlisting criteria: 1 mark for each completed year of relevant experience beyond the minimum requirement (1/365 mark per additional day for incomplete years); 1 mark for each additional relevant degree over the minimum essential qualification, up to a maximum of 2 marks. HCL may add further criteria if required.

Document Verification

  • Interview intimation is communicated by email only; call letters are issued to shortlisted candidates.
  • Requests to change the interview/test date, time or venue once communicated will not be entertained.

  • Original documents (as listed under Documents Required below) will be verified at the interview; non-production of originals will debar the candidate from appearing.

  4. Submit the application to receive your Application Number.
  5. Print the Computer-Generated Online Application and the Acknowledgement Slip, and keep copies for your records.
Important: No hard copy of the application is accepted. Applications are screened purely on the information furnished online, without document verification at that stage, so candidates must ensure they genuinely meet all eligibility criteria before applying. Submit well in advance of the closing date.

  • Experience Certificate for each declared organization, containing Designation, Department, Date of Joining, Date of Leaving, and job description/responsibility (date-specific if responsibility changed)
  • Salary Slip & Bank Statement for the last 3 months / PF Statement / Appointment Letter and latest Form-16 of the last employment
  • Any Statutory Certificate defined under the eligibility criteria for the applied discipline (e.g., MCI registration for M&HS, Surveyor Certificate of Competency for Survey)
  • CGPA/GPA/SGPA-to-percentage conversion certificate from the University/Institute, where letter grades were awarded
  • Caste/Category Certificate in the Government of India prescribed format, for SC/OBC (Non-Creamy Layer) candidates; OBC (NCL) certificate must be issued on or after 01.04.2026 (a certificate issued before that date may be used at application stage, subject to producing the valid one at joining)
  • Self-certified English/Hindi translation of the SC/OBC certificate, if originally issued in another language
  • Minimum any 2 of: Appointment Letter/Pay Slip/Form-16/PF Statement/Bank Statement (towards salary credit), for each declared employment, to be uploaded in the online application itself

Important Conditions

  • Application Fee: General & OBC candidates pay a non-refundable ₹500/- processing fee; SC/PwBD candidates are exempted. Fee (plus applicable bank charges) must be paid only via Payment Gateway/NEFT online transfer through HCL’s website – no other remittance mode is accepted.
  • Appointment is subject to the candidate being found medically fit by a Medical Authority prescribed by HCL Management.
  • Travelling ticket fare (from the correspondence address to the interview venue) is reimbursed only for candidates who are actually interviewed; those found ineligible at document verification are not eligible for reimbursement.
  • The services of the incumbent are purely temporary/contractual and do not confer any right or claim to regular employment, absorption, or regularization in HCL.
  • Appointment remains provisional until caste/category certificates and other testimonials are verified; false claims lead to termination and possible further action.
  • Category (SC/OBC-NCL) once declared in the online application cannot be changed, and no benefit of another category will be admissible during the process.
  • Email ID and mobile number provided must remain active until the recruitment process is complete; the email ID cannot be changed once entered. All correspondence is via email only.
  • Any canvassing, direct or indirect, disqualifies the candidature. Legal jurisdiction for any dispute is Kolkata only.
  • In case of conflict between the Hindi and English versions of the advertisement, the English version prevails.
  • HCL reserves the right to fill, not fill, or partly fill any post, and to cancel/restrict/modify/alter the recruitment process without assigning any reason.
  • Selected candidates are liable to serve anywhere in India, including other locations/units of the Company, and may be assigned to similar projects during the contract.

SBI SCO Recruitment 2026-27 Overview

Particulars Details
Recruiting Organisation State Bank of India (SBI), Central Recruitment & Promotion Department, Corporate Centre, Mumbai

Event Date

Last Date for Online Registration & Fee Payment 06.10.2026
Cut-off Date for Age, Qualification & Experience 31.08.2026
Interview Date Not specified in the notification; call letters will be sent by email only

SBI SCO Recruitment 2026-27 Vacancy Details

Advertisement No. CRPD/SCO/2026-27/20 - SBIL, Kolkata

Post PwBD (VI) Total Age (Min–Max)
Dean, SBIL Kolkata 1 (within UR) 1 40–55 years

Combined Grand Total: 7 posts across both notifications. PwBD reservation is horizontal and included within the respective parent category (UR/SC) - it is not an additional vacancy over the stated total. Reserved-category candidates (including PwBD) for whom no reservation is indicated are free to apply against Unreserved (UR) vacancies, provided they meet the UR eligibility criteria. The number of vacancies, including reserved vacancies, is provisional and may vary as per the Bank's actual requirement.

SBI SCO Recruitment 2026-27 Eligibility Criteria

Advt No. 20 - SBIL, Kolkata Posts

Post Basic Educational Qualification Post-Qualification Experience
Dean MBA / Executive MBA / PGDM / PGDBA or equivalent in any discipline (min. 55% marks), OR Ph.D./M.Phil. from an Indian university or Indian/International 'B' school Total 15 years' post-qualification experience, including minimum 3 years as Dean/Deputy Dean/Principal/Director/Deputy Director/Joint Director/Head/Centre Head/Chief Learning Officer/Senior VP/VP or equivalent in a Bank's Training Institute/University/Business School/Corporate Learning Academy/Public Sector Training Institution/Other Educational Institution
Faculty Postgraduate in any discipline (min. 55% marks); successful completion of Ph.D./M.Phil. is an additional qualification Minimum 6 years' teaching experience as Faculty/Professor/Assistant Professor/Associate Professor/Corporate Trainer or equivalent in a Bank's Training Institute/University/Business School/Corporate Learning Academy/Public Sector Training Institution/Other Educational Institution
Marketing Executive MBA or equivalent in Marketing (min. 55% marks) Minimum 5 years' experience in Marketing, of which minimum 3 years in marketing of Executive Education/Management Institutes/Universities/Training Organizations/EdTech Organizations

Preference for Dean and Faculty posts is given to candidates with an MBA/Ph.D./M.Phil. in Banking & Finance and/or teaching experience in Executive Education, and to those with proven experience in Corporate Leadership Roles. For Marketing Executive, preference is given to candidates with experience in branding, international partnerships, programme portfolio generation, and revenue generation.

Advt No. 22 - IT Risk Posts

Post Basic Educational Qualification Preferred Certifications Post-Qualification Experience
Deputy Vice President (IT Risk) BE/BTech (Computer Science/Electronics & Communications/IT/Cybersecurity), min. 50% marks, OR MCA/MSc (Computer Science)/MSc (IT), min. 50%, OR MTech (Computer Science/Cyber Security/Information Security), min. 50% Any one of CISSP, CRISC, CISM, or CISA (valid, dated on or before last date of registration) Minimum 12 years in the IT Domain, of which minimum 6 years in IT risk management or information security is preferable
Assistant Vice President (IT Risk) Same as above Same as above Minimum 9 years in the IT Domain, of which minimum 5 years in IT risk management or information security is preferable

Note: Training/teaching experience will NOT be counted for eligibility for the IT Risk posts. Candidates cannot apply for both IT Risk posts (Deputy VP and AVP) - only the last valid application will be retained if a candidate applies to both, and the fee paid for the other registration will be forfeited.

For all posts, the prescribed qualification is a minimum requirement - the candidate must possess the required post-basic qualification and relevant full-time experience as on the specified dates. The relevant experience certificate from the employer must specifically state that the candidate had experience in the required field. Where the degree/diploma/PG certificate does not specify the field of specialization, the candidate must produce a certificate from the concerned university/college specifically mentioning the specialization.

SBI SCO Recruitment 2026-27 Age Limit

Post Minimum Age Maximum Age
Dean, SBIL Kolkata 40 years 55 years
Faculty, SBIL Kolkata 35 years 55 years
Marketing Executive, SBIL Kolkata 28 years 40 years
Deputy Vice President (IT Risk) 36 years 45 years
Assistant Vice President (IT Risk) 32 years 42 years

Age is reckoned as on 31.08.2026. The maximum age indicated is for Unreserved (UR) category candidates. Relaxation in the upper age limit is available to reserved category candidates, including PwBD, as per Government of India guidelines. Candidates seeking age relaxation must submit copies of the necessary certificates at the time of document verification - no change in category is permitted after registration of the online application.

Candidates are advised to check whether they satisfy the prescribed age limit before applying. Use our online Age Calculator to calculate your exact age instantly.

SBI SCO Recruitment 2026-27 Remuneration / CTC

Post Annual CTC (Negotiable)
Dean, SBIL Kolkata Up to ₹98 lakhs
Faculty, SBIL Kolkata Up to ₹63 lakhs
Marketing Executive, SBIL Kolkata ₹52 lakhs
Deputy Vice President (IT Risk) Up to ₹60 lakhs
Assistant Vice President (IT Risk) Up to ₹50 lakhs

Annual CTC is negotiable and depends on the candidate's experience, current emoluments, and place of posting. CTC is bifurcated into Fixed Pay and Variable Pay in an 80:20 ratio, and includes an option for accommodation (and a vehicle, for SBIL posts) - where accommodation/vehicle is availed, a notional amount is deducted from the CTC. Variable pay is subject to securing a minimum qualifying score in the half-yearly performance appraisal (90% or more for full variable pay eligibility under Advt No. 20). Annual increment from the second year onward can be up to 10% of the finalized annual CTC (Advt No. 20) or up to 7% (Advt No. 22), subject to a minimum performance appraisal score of 90%.

SBI SCO Recruitment 2026-27 Application Fee

Category Fee (Non-refundable)
General / EWS / OBC ₹750
SC / ST / PwBD Nil

Fee payment is via Internet Banking, Debit Card, Credit Card, or UPI through the payment gateway integrated with the online application. Transaction charges, if any, are borne by the candidate. The application fee, once paid, is non-refundable and cannot be adjusted against any other examination or selection in future. Candidates seeking fee exemption (SC/ST/PwBD) must submit a valid caste/disability certificate in the Government of India-prescribed format at the time of document verification.

SBI SCO Recruitment 2026-27 Selection Process

For Dean and Faculty Posts (Advt No. 20)

  • Shortlisting, followed by Interview cum Demo Session.
  • Interview/Demo Session carries 100 marks; the qualifying marks are decided by the Bank.

For Marketing Executive (Advt No. 20) and Both IT Risk Posts (Advt No. 22)

  • Shortlisting, followed by Interview.

Common Selection Process (Both Notifications)

  • Shortlisting: A shortlisting committee constituted by the Bank decides the shortlisting parameters; merely fulfilling minimum qualification and experience does not entitle a candidate to be called for interview. The Bank's decision is final, with no correspondence entertained.
  • CTC Negotiation: Conducted with candidates in order of merit, one by one. If a selected candidate does not agree to the negotiated CTC, they are treated as a Voluntary Exit, and the next candidate in the merit list is called for negotiation.
  • Merit List: Prepared in descending order based on interview marks only. In case of a tie at the cut-off, candidates are ranked by age in descending order (older candidate ranked higher).
  • Final Selection: Top-most candidates in the merit list with whom CTC negotiation is successful are finally selected.

Shortlisting is provisional and without verification of original documents; candidature is subject to verification of all details/documents against originals at the time of interview. If a candidate called for interview/CTC negotiation is found not satisfying the eligibility criteria (age, educational qualification, experience, etc.), they will not be allowed to appear for interview, and no travelling expenses will be reimbursed.

SBI SCO Recruitment 2026-27 Contract Terms

  • Contract Period: 3 years, extendable up to a maximum of 2 further years at the Bank's discretion (total engagement not to exceed 5 years).
  • Notice Period: The contract can be terminated without assigning any reason, by giving 3 months' notice from either side, or by payment/surrender of 3 months' compensation in lieu thereof.
  • Leave (Advt No. 20 posts): Officers Engaged on Contract (OECs) are entitled to 30 days' leave during the financial year, granted for genuine and appropriate reasons.

How to Apply for SBI SCO Recruitment 2026-27

  1. Register online through the link on SBI's official website, https://sbi.bank.in/web/careers/current-openings.
  2. Scan your latest photograph and signature in the specified format before starting the application - the online application will not register without these uploads.
  3. Fill in the application form carefully. You may save partially completed information; a provisional registration number and password will be generated - editing the saved application is allowed up to three times.
  4. Upload all required documents: Resume, ID proof, Age proof, Caste Certificate (if applicable), PwBD Certificate (if applicable), Educational Qualification certificates, other qualifications/certifications, proof of experience, Biodata, and CTC Form.
  5. Once the application is completely filled, submit it and proceed to online fee payment (if applicable) via Debit Card/Credit Card/Internet Banking/UPI.
  6. On successful payment, an e-receipt and application form bearing the submission date will be generated - print and retain this for your records.
  7. Complete registration and fee payment before the closing date, 06.10.2026. The registration process is complete only when the fee is deposited on or before this date.

Candidates should have a valid Email ID and active mobile number, kept functional until declaration of results and issuance of call letters, since all communication (call letters, interview advice) will be sent only by email - no hard copy will be sent.

SBI SCO Recruitment 2026-27 Important Instructions

  • The Bank reserves the right to change the notified vacancies, including reserved vacancies, without assigning any reason.
  • The Bank reserves the right to cancel or modify the engagement process, entirely or partially, at any stage, without assigning any reason, and will not refund the fee or pay compensation in such an event.
  • Candidates furnishing false information or suppressing facts will be disqualified and liable for debarment and legal/criminal action.
  • Candidates serving in Government/Quasi-Government offices, Public Sector Undertakings (including Nationalized Banks and Financial Institutions) must submit a 'No Objection Certificate' from their employer at the time of interview, failing which their candidature will not be considered and travelling expenses (if otherwise admissible) will not be paid.
  • Selected candidates must produce a proper discharge certificate from their current employer at the time of taking up the engagement.
  • The Bank reserves the right to post/transfer engaged officers to any office of SBI in India, or depute them to any associate/subsidiary or other organization, depending on service requirements. Requests for a specific posting location will not be entertained.
  • Candidates are advised to apply well before the closing date to avoid last-minute website load issues; SBI is not responsible for failure to submit an application due to such reasons.
  • All updates, revisions, corrigenda, results, and shortlisting/selection lists will be hosted only on the Bank's website - no separate intimation will be issued.
  • Candidates against whom there are adverse reports regarding character, antecedents, or moral turpitude are not eligible to apply; if such reports are received after selection, the candidature/engagement will be rejected forthwith.
  • Mere fulfilment of the minimum eligibility criteria (qualification and experience) does not entitle a candidate to be called for interview.

What Is a Bharat Sarkari Job?

A Bharat Sarkari Job is any government job opportunity offered across India's central and state government departments - spanning all 28 states and 8 union territories. The term "Bharat" simply emphasises pan-India coverage: a Bharat Sarkari Job notification could originate from a central body like the SSC, UPSC, or Indian Railways, or from a state public service commission recruiting for state-level posts. Regardless of origin, these roles share the defining traits Indian aspirants seek - long-term job security, government pay scales, and statutory retirement benefits.

Sarkari Job vs Private Job

A sarkari job differs from private-sector employment in a few important ways: government positions are governed by service rules that protect against arbitrary termination, salaries follow Pay Commission recommendations rather than market negotiation, and employees are entitled to pension schemes (NPS or OPS depending on recruitment year), medical coverage under CGHS, and fixed working hours. Private jobs, by contrast, often offer higher starting pay in competitive fields but carry less structural job security.

Sarkari Bharat Vacancies by Sector

Sarkari bharat vacancies span several major recruiting sectors. Each sector below links to a dedicated hub page with sector-specific notifications, eligibility criteria, and exam patterns.

Banking Jobs (IBPS, SBI, RBI)

Banking recruitment includes IBPS PO, IBPS Clerk, SBI PO, SBI Clerk, RBI Assistant, and NABARD postings. These roles are among the most competitive sarkari bharat jobs, offering strong starting pay and clear promotion tracks. Browse current openings on our Banking Jobs hub.

Railway Jobs (RRB NTPC, ALP, Group D)

Indian Railways is the country's largest single recruiter, with RRB NTPC, Group D, ALP, JE, and Technician posts opening in large batches. Check live Railway vacancies on our Railway Jobs hub.

Defence Jobs (Army, Navy, Air Force)

Defence recruitment covers Indian Army (including Agniveer), Navy, Air Force, BSF, CRPF, CISF, and ITBP postings. See ongoing openings on our Defence Jobs hub.

Teaching Jobs (KVS, NVS, State Boards)

Teaching sarkari jobs include KVS, NVS, DSSSB, and state education board recruitment for TGT, PGT, and PRT posts. Explore current teaching vacancies on our Teaching Jobs hub.

SSC & UPSC Notifications

SSC (CGL, CHSL, MTS, GD) and UPSC (Civil Services, CDS, NDA) notifications remain the most closely tracked central-government exams. Full notification archives are available on our SSC Jobs and UPSC Jobs hubs.

Sarkari Job Find - Filter by Qualification & State

Not every sarkari job requires a degree. Use the qualification and state filters below to sarkari job find openings that actually match your eligibility, instead of scrolling through listings you don't qualify for.

Several high-volume recruiters - including Railways (Group D), SSC (MTS, GD), and state police departments - recruit primarily at the 10th pass and 12th pass level. Browse these openings on our 10th & 12th Pass Jobs page.

Sarkari Job for Graduates & Postgraduates

Graduate and postgraduate-level sarkari jobs include SSC CGL, Bank PO, UPSC Civil Services, and various state PCS exams. See qualification-matched listings on our Graduate Jobs page.

State-Wise Sarkari Bharat Job (Bihar, UP, Tamil Nadu, and more)

State government recruitment is listed separately by state, since eligibility and domicile rules vary. Find your state's current openings via our State Government Jobs directory.

सरकारी फॉर्म ऑनलाइन 2026 कैसे भरें? (How to Apply Online)

हर साल लाखों उम्मीदवार सरकारी फॉर्म ऑनलाइन 2026 भरने की प्रक्रिया में गलतियाँ कर बैठते हैं, जिससे उनका आवेदन रद्द हो सकता है। नीचे दी गई सरल प्रक्रिया से आप अपना फॉर्म सही तरीके से भर सकते हैं।

आवेदन की चरणबद्ध प्रक्रिया

  1. संबंधित विभाग की आधिकारिक अधिसूचना (Notification PDF) ध्यान से पढ़ें और अपनी पात्रता जांचें।
  2. वैध ईमेल आईडी और मोबाइल नंबर से पोर्टल पर पंजीकरण (Registration) करें।
  3. व्यक्तिगत विवरण, शैक्षणिक योग्यता, और आवश्यक दस्तावेज़ अपलोड करें (फोटो, हस्ताक्षर, प्रमाणपत्र)।
  4. निर्धारित आवेदन शुल्क का ऑनलाइन भुगतान करें और भुगतान की रसीद सुरक्षित रखें।
  5. फॉर्म सबमिट करने से पहले सभी जानकारी की दोबारा जांच करें और फॉर्म का प्रिंटआउट अवश्य लें।

Documents Required for Sarkari Form

Typical documents needed: recent passport-size photograph (as per specified size/format), scanned signature, educational certificates and mark sheets, category certificate (if applicable), and a valid ID proof (Aadhaar/PAN).

Common Mistakes to Avoid While Applying

  • Submitting a photo or signature that doesn't match the specified pixel/size requirements.
  • Missing the last date due to server load - apply at least 2–3 days before deadline.
  • Entering a name or date of birth that doesn't match your certificates exactly.
  • Forgetting to download and save the final submitted form and payment receipt.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is a Bharat Sarkari Job?

A Bharat Sarkari Job refers to any government job opportunity across India's central and state departments - including Railways, Banking, SSC, UPSC, Defence, Police, and PSUs - offering job security, fixed pay scales, and pension benefits under government service rules.

How can I get instant Sarkari Job Alert notifications?

You can bookmark this page for daily updates, or subscribe to OnlyJobs's notification service to receive a Sarkari Job Alert as soon as a new central or state vacancy is announced.

Where can I check the latest Bharat Job Result 2026?

All declared results - including written exam results, merit lists, and interview outcomes - are listed in the Results section of this page, updated as soon as departments release official Bharat Job Result notices.

How do I find a Sarkari Job that matches my qualification?

Use the qualification filters on this page to sarkari job find openings suited to 10th pass, 12th pass, diploma, graduate, or postgraduate candidates, sorted by sector and state.

सरकारी फॉर्म ऑनलाइन 2026 में आवेदन कैसे करें?

सबसे पहले संबंधित विभाग की आधिकारिक अधिसूचना पढ़ें, पात्रता जांचें, फिर वैध ईमेल और मोबाइल नंबर से रजिस्ट्रेशन करके फॉर्म भरें, दस्तावेज़ अपलोड करें और आवेदन शुल्क जमा करें।

Is OnlyJobs reliable for sarkarijob updates?

Yes - OnlyJobs has tracked sarkarijob notifications since 2011, cross-verifying every listing against official department websites before publishing.

What is the difference between a Sarkari Job and a private-sector job?

Sarkari jobs offer government-backed job security, pension (NPS/OPS), fixed working hours, and statutory benefits, while private jobs typically offer market-driven pay with fewer long-term security guarantees.

Anganwadi Recruitment 2026 – FAQ's

How to apply for Anganwadi Recruitment 2026 online?

Visit your state's official WCD / ICDS portal (link provided in table above). Register with mobile & Aadhaar, fill the application form, upload documents (photo, 10th certificate, Aadhaar, domicile), and submit before the last date. Print the application acknowledgement slip after submission.

What is the eligibility for Anganwadi Worker 2026?

Candidates must have passed 10th or 12th standard from a recognized board. Age limit is 18–35 years (varies by state). Must be a permanent resident of the ward/village for which vacancy exists. Only female candidates are eligible for Worker and Helper posts.

What is the salary of Anganwadi Worker in 2026?

Anganwadi Worker receives a monthly honorarium of ₹10,000–₹20,000 depending on the state (Karnataka and TN are highest at ~₹14,000). Anganwadi Helper gets ₹5,000–₹7,000/month. The Central Government pays ₹4,500/month as base honorarium, and states add their own component on top.

Is there a written exam for Anganwadi jobs?

No, there is no written examination for Anganwadi Worker and Anganwadi Helper posts. Selection is purely merit-based on academic qualification marks (10th / 12th percentage). For Supervisor / CDPO posts, a written exam or interview may be conducted depending on the state.

What is the age limit for Anganwadi Helper?

Age limit is 18 to 35 years as of 1st January 2026 in most states. SC/ST candidates get 5 years relaxation (maximum age 40). OBC candidates get 3 years relaxation (maximum age 38). PwD candidates get additional relaxation as per state rules.

What documents are required for Anganwadi job application?

Required documents: Aadhaar card, 10th/12th marksheet and certificate, domicile/residence certificate, caste certificate (SC/ST/OBC), passport-size photograph, scanned signature, and EWS/PwD certificate if applicable. Graduation certificate is needed for Supervisor post applications.

What is ICDS recruitment 2026?

ICDS stands for Integrated Child Development Services - the government programme under which Anganwadi centres operate nationwide. ICDS recruitment 2026 refers to hiring of Anganwadi Workers, Helpers, Supervisors, and CDPOs by state WCD departments under the Ministry of Women & Child Development (wcd.nic.in).

Is Anganwadi Worker a permanent government job?

Anganwadi Workers and Helpers are honorary workers, not regular government employees. They receive a fixed monthly honorarium (not salary) and are entitled to benefits like ESI, health insurance, and maternity benefits. Supervisors and CDPOs are regular government employees in most states and receive full pay & grade pay.

Can I apply for Anganwadi job from a different district?

No. Anganwadi Workers and Helpers must be permanent residents of the same ward/village/district where the vacancy exists. A domicile or residence certificate is mandatory. Applications from outside the specified locality are rejected. For Supervisor/CDPO posts, the same district residency rule generally applies.

Forest Department Posts List

The forest department offers a range of posts across different levels, from ground-level field roles to gazetted officer positions. Most current openings on this page are for Group C posts - Forest Guard, Forester, Beat Guard, and Field Guard - making this a common landing point for anyone searching forest department group c recruitment 2026.

  • Forest Guard - entry-level field post responsible for forest protection and anti-poaching patrols
  • Forester - supervises Forest Guards and manages a forest beat or range sub-unit
  • Forest Beat Officer - field-level post combining patrol, record-keeping, and community liaison duties; commonly searched as forest beat officer notification 2026
  • Range Forest Officer (RFO) - manages an entire forest range, includes administrative and enforcement responsibilities
  • Assistant Conservator of Forests (ACF) - gazetted officer post, typically recruited through state forest service exams
  • Indian Forest Service (IFS) Officer - recruited through UPSC, the highest field-level forestry cadre in India

Eligibility for Forest Department Jobs 2026

Educational Qualification

  • Forest Guard / Forest Watcher / Field Guard: 10th or 12th pass from a recognized board
  • Forester: 12th pass, often with Science subjects; some states require a diploma in Forestry
  • Range Forest Officer: Graduate degree, frequently in Science, Agriculture, or Forestry
  • ACF / IFS: Graduate degree in a relevant discipline (Botany, Zoology, Forestry, Agriculture, Veterinary Science, Engineering, or Environmental Science), followed by the respective state or UPSC exam

Age Limit & Relaxation

The general age limit for Forest Guard and Forester posts is usually 18–27 years, though this varies by state. Age relaxation is generally available for SC/ST (5 years), OBC (3 years), PwBD candidates, and other reserved categories as per government norms.

Reservation & Age Relaxation for Ex-Servicemen

Most state forest departments reserve a fixed percentage of Forest Guard, Forester, and Beat Guard posts for ex-servicemen, in addition to SC, ST, OBC, and EWS reservations. Candidates applying for jobs for ex servicemen in forest department typically receive:

  • Additional age relaxation, usually 3–5 years beyond the general age cap (or as per length of military service)
  • Relaxed physical standards in several states
  • A reserved vacancy quota, separate from the general merit list

Exact quota percentages and relaxation norms differ by state, so always cross-check the specific notification before applying.

Physical Standards

Most Forest Guard and Forester posts require candidates to clear height, chest measurement (for male candidates), and a Physical Efficiency Test involving running, walking, or trekking - since the job involves regular field patrol duty in forest terrain.

Selection Process & Exam Pattern for Forest Officer & Forest Guard Posts

The selection process for forest department recruitment generally involves multiple stages, designed to test both academic knowledge and physical fitness given the field nature of the job.

Written Exam, PET/PST & Document Verification

  1. Written Examination - objective-type questions on General Knowledge, General Science, Reasoning, Mathematics, and sometimes Forestry/Environment-related topics
  2. Physical Efficiency Test (PET) / Physical Standard Test (PST) - running, walking/trekking distance, height and chest measurement
  3. Document Verification - verification of educational certificates, age proof, category certificates, and (where applicable) ex-servicemen discharge documents
  4. Medical Examination - fitness check before final appointment
  5. Final Merit List - based on combined written exam and PET/PST scores, as per each state's weightage formula

Syllabus Highlights for Forest Guard & Ranger

  • General Knowledge & Current Affairs
  • General Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology basics)
  • Basic Mathematics / Numerical Ability
  • Reasoning & Mental Ability
  • State-specific General Knowledge (local geography, forests, wildlife sanctuaries)
  • For Ranger/RFO level: Forestry science, environmental laws, and wildlife protection acts

Note: Apprenticeship posts (under the Apprentices Act) are not regular government jobs but are a popular no-exam entry route into PSUs and railways for ITI/diploma/graduate candidates, offering valuable hands-on experience.

Two Types of No Exam Govt Jobs

No-exam recruitment in India falls into two patterns, and knowing which one a notification belongs to tells you exactly what to prepare for:

Type Typical Posts Who it's for How Selection Works
Fresher - no exam, usually no interview Apprentice, GDS, trainee 10th/12th/ITI/Diploma/Graduate pass Merit list prepared from academic marks
Experienced - no exam, interview-based Officer, manager, specialist, medical Professionals with relevant work experience Shortlisting based on qualification/experience, followed by a personal interview

How Recruitment Without Exam Works in Government Jobs

This section explains the different routes through which government departments fill vacancies without conducting a written competitive exam.

1. Direct Recruitment

Certain senior and specialised posts - such as Chairman, Member, and Secretary in Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) and State Public Service Commissions (PSCs) - are filled through direct recruitment based on eligibility criteria like qualifications, experience, and domain expertise, rather than a written exam. Similarly, some administrative posts in the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) may be filled through direct recruitment.

2. Sports Quota Recruitment

Government organisations such as Indian Railways, the Indian Army, and Public Sector Banks reserve a quota of posts for candidates with outstanding achievements in sports at the state, national, or international level. Eligible candidates can be appointed to posts like Assistant Station Master, Ticket Collector, and Clerk without going through the regular written exam.

3. Cultural Quota Recruitment

Indian Railways also recruits individuals with exceptional talent in arts, fine arts, music, or literature under the cultural quota for posts such as Junior Clerk, Ticket Collector, and Assistant Loco Pilot.

4. Internal Promotions and Deputation

Government departments, including the Indian Administrative Service (IAS) and Indian Police Service (IPS), promote existing employees to higher posts based on performance, seniority, and experience - without requiring them to clear a fresh competitive exam. Ex-servicemen and defence personnel are also often considered for civilian government posts through deputation or reservation quotas, without a written exam.

5. Apprenticeships and Trainee Programmes

Railways, PSUs, and central organisations like DRDO and BEL regularly hire Act Apprentices, Trade Apprentices, and Project Trainees through merit lists based on academic marks - with no written entrance test.

6. Walk-in Interviews

Some government and PSU organisations directly call candidates for walk-in interviews based on their qualifications and experience, especially for technical, medical, and contractual roles.

Government Jobs Without Exam by Sector

This section breaks down no-exam opportunities by sector - banking and railways - which are among the most common areas where such recruitment occurs.

Bank Jobs Without Exam

While most public sector bank recruitment (PO, Clerk, SO) happens through IBPS or bank-specific written exams, some banks fill specific posts - such as Local Bank Officer and certain Specialist Officer roles - through direct recruitment, where the bank shortlists applications based on eligibility criteria and conducts an interview instead of a written test.

Railway Jobs Without Exam

Indian Railways and the various Railway Recruitment Boards/Cells (RRBs/RRCs) offer no-exam entry through:

  • Act Apprentices (selection via academic merit list)
  • Sports Quota posts (Assistant Station Master, Ticket Collector, Clerk)
  • Cultural Quota posts (Junior Clerk, Ticket Collector, Assistant Loco Pilot)
  • Scouts and Guides Quota

Before You Apply: How to Spot Fake "No Exam" Job Offers

No-exam recruitment is the single biggest magnet for job fraud in India, because "direct joining, no exam" is exactly what scammers promise. Four rules protect you:

  1. No genuine government post is ever sold. Nobody - agent, "officer", consultancy - can arrange selection for money. The only payment in real recruitment is the application fee, paid on the official portal, typically a few hundred rupees.
  2. Verify the notification on the official domain. Every real notice lives on a .gov.in, .nic.in or official PSU domain. Every row in our list links to the post page where the official notification PDF and apply link are attached - if an offer you received isn't traceable to an official notice, treat it as fraud.
  3. No recruitment happens over WhatsApp or Telegram DMs. Forwarded "joining letters" and interview calls demanding a deposit are scams, full stop.
  4. Cross-check suspicious notices against PIB Fact Check before sharing or paying anything.

How to Apply for Government Jobs Without Exam

  1. Open the post from the live list and read the official notification PDF - eligibility, age limits and fee are final there, not in any summary.
  2. Confirm you match the qualification and category requirements before paying any fee.
  3. Apply on the official portal linked in the notification; keep the registration number and fee receipt.
  4. For merit-list posts (GDS, apprentice), enter marks exactly as on your certificates - mismatches reject applications at verification.
  5. Track the post page for merit list / shortlist updates, or subscribe to WhatsApp/Telegram alerts so deadlines and results reach you automatically.

Government Jobs Without Exam - FAQs

1. Are there really government jobs without an exam?

Yes. Apprenticeship intakes, India Post GDS, sports and cultural quota posts, walk-in interviews and direct recruitment for experienced candidates are all filled without a written competitive exam. The live list at the top of this page shows every such notification currently open.

2. Which government jobs have no exam and no interview at all?

India Post GDS and Railway/PSU Act Apprentice selections use only a merit list of academic marks - there is no written test and no interview. Everything depends on your Class 10 (and ITI/diploma, where applicable) percentage.

3. What no-exam options exist for freshers after 10th, 12th or ITI?

Apprenticeships, GDS and trainee posts are the main fresher routes. Selection is a merit list prepared from academic marks, which is why these notifications attract very high application volumes despite no exam.

4. Can experienced professionals get a government job without an exam?

Yes. PSUs and autonomous bodies fill officer, manager and specialist posts by shortlisting candidates on qualification and experience, followed by a personal interview - no written test.

5. Are government jobs without exam permanent?

Often not. Apprenticeships are roughly one-year training engagements with a stipend, and many walk-in posts are contractual with fixed tenure. Direct-recruitment posts can be regular - the notification states the nature of each post, so check before applying.

6. Are there bank jobs without an exam?

A few. Some banks fill specialist and local officer posts through shortlisting plus interview. Bank apprenticeship drives vary - some are merit-based while others include an online test - so read each notification's selection clause.

7. Are there railway jobs without an exam?

Yes: Act Apprentice intakes (merit list), sports quota, cultural quota and Scouts & Guides quota. Apprentice intakes are large; the quota routes are small zonal recruitments with their own assessment process.

8. Is India Post GDS really without an exam?

Yes - selection is an online merit list generated from Class 10 marks, with no exam and no interview. Because of that, GDS is heavily targeted by paid-selection scams; apply only through the official GDS portal.

9. How do I identify fake "no exam" job offers?

No genuine government post is sold, fees are paid only on official portals, and no recruitment happens over WhatsApp or Telegram messages. Verify every offer against the official notification on a government or PSU domain - if it isn't there, it's fraud.

10. How often is this list updated?

Daily. New notifications are added as they release, and every listing is removed automatically after its last date, so the list only ever shows posts you can still apply for.

Govt Jobs for Law Graduates - Eligibility (LLB, LLM, BL)

Eligibility varies by post, but the core requirement for almost every government law job is a recognised law degree. Senior and specialised roles add experience, an LLM, or Bar enrolment on top.

Educational Qualification

  • Bachelor of Law (BL) / LLB (Legum Baccalaureus): the baseline qualification for most legal and law officer posts.
  • LLM (Master of Laws): required for senior legal officer, faculty, and some advisory positions.
  • Integrated 5-year degrees - BA LLB, BBA LLB, BCom LLB - are accepted wherever an LLB is required.

The degree must be from a university recognised by the Bar Council of India.

Bar Council Enrolment & AIBE

For litigation, prosecutor, and standing-counsel roles you generally need to be enrolled as an advocate with a State Bar Council, and many positions ask for the All India Bar Examination (AIBE) Certificate of Practice issued by the Bar Council of India. Purely advisory or research posts (Law Clerk, Research Fellow, Legal Consultant) often do not require enrolment.

Age Limit & Relaxations

The upper age limit is typically 30 to 40 years for the general category, depending on the post and recruiter. Statutory relaxations apply: usually 3 years for OBC, 5 years for SC/ST, and additional relaxation for PwD and ex-servicemen candidates. Always confirm the exact limit and cut-off date in the official notification, as judicial-service and PSU limits differ.

Salary & Pay Scale for Government Law Jobs

Pay depends on the organisation and grade. Officer-level legal posts under the 7th Pay Commission generally fall in Pay Levels 10 to 12, with a monthly salary roughly between ₹56,100 and ₹1,77,500, plus Dearness Allowance, House Rent Allowance, and other benefits. PSU legal officers are paid on IDA scales, which can be higher at entry grade.

Types of Law Officer / Legal Posts in Government Sector

  • Judicial Services - Civil Judge (Junior Division), Additional District Judge, High Court Judge, recruited via State Judicial Service Exams (PCS-J)
  • Law Officer / Legal Officer - Roles in public sector banks (IBPS SO Law), insurance companies (LIC AAO Legal), regulatory bodies (SEBI Grade A Legal), and PSUs (Coal India, NTPC, GAIL Legal)
  • Legal Assistant & Legal Advisor - Administrative legal support roles in ministries, universities, and district courts
  • Assistant Public Prosecutor (APO) - Prosecution roles recruited through State PSCs, requiring LLB and often a minimum years of practice

Judicial Services (Civil Judge, ADJ, High Court Judge)

Judicial Services is the most prestigious and highest-paying career path for LLB graduates. Recruitment happens through State Public Service Commissions (e.g., RPSC, UPPSC, MPPSC) via a three-stage exam: Preliminary, Mains, and Interview. Civil Judge posts typically require 0-3 years of practice depending on the state, while some states allow fresh LLB graduates to apply directly.

Law Officer / Legal Officer (Banks, PSU, Insurance)

Public sector banks and insurance companies recruit Law Officers through specialist officer (SO) exams. These posts require only an LLB degree (AIBE not mandatory) and offer competitive pay scales under the 7th Pay Commission equivalent structure, along with allowances.

Legal Assistant & Legal Advisor Posts

These are typically Group B/C administrative-legal posts in ministries, universities, and PSU legal departments, requiring an LLB degree and sometimes relevant drafting/litigation experience.

Assistant Public Prosecutor (APO)

APO recruitment is conducted by State PSCs (e.g., RPSC Assistant Prosecution Officer) and requires an LLB degree, enrollment as an advocate, and in most states, a minimum period of practice (often 3 years).

Selection Process for Law Govt Jobs

The selection process differs by post but commonly includes:

  1. Written examination - testing legal knowledge, aptitude, and general awareness (for judicial services and most exam-based posts).
  2. Interview / viva-voce - assessing legal reasoning and suitability.
  3. Document verification - degree, Bar enrolment, AIBE, age, and category certificates.

Advisory and consultant posts are often filled by shortlisting and interview alone, without a written exam.

Law Govt Jobs FAQ's

What are the latest law govt jobs in 2026?

Current law government jobs in 2026 include Law Officer, Legal Officer, Assistant Prosecution Officer, Judicial Service, and Legal Adviser posts across High Courts, PSUs, public sector banks, and central/state departments. The table above is updated daily with vacancy count, last date, and the official notification link.

Which departments hire LLB and law graduates?

High Courts and District Courts, the Ministry of Law and Justice, UPSC, State Public Service Commissions, public sector banks, PSUs, insurance companies, and regulatory bodies regularly recruit law graduates for legal and judicial roles.

What is the eligibility for government law jobs?

Most posts require a Bachelor of Law (LLB/BL) from a recognised university; senior roles may require LLM and experience. Litigation and prosecutor posts usually require enrolment with a State Bar Council and, often, the AIBE certificate.

What is the salary of a Law Officer in the government sector?

A government Law Officer or Legal Officer typically earns between ₹56,100 and ₹1,77,500 per month under the 7th Pay Commission, depending on the organisation, plus DA, HRA, and allowances. PSU legal officers draw IDA-scale pay.

Can a fresher LLB graduate get a government job?

Yes. Freshers can apply for Civil Judge (Junior Division) judicial-service exams, Law Clerk and Research Fellow posts in High Courts, and trainee legal roles. Some PSU and bank Law Officer posts require a few years of post-enrolment experience.

How can I apply for law officer vacancies in central government?

Open the post in the table above, read the official notification, register on the recruiter's portal, fill in the application with your LLB and enrolment details, pay the fee, and submit before the last date.

What is the difference between Judicial Services and Law Officer posts

Judicial Services (Civil Judge, via state judiciary exams) places you on the bench as a judge. Law Officer/Legal Officer posts are departmental legal-counsel roles in PSUs, banks, and ministries - advisory and litigation support, recruited by interview or written test.

Is there an age limit for govt law jobs?

Most posts set the upper age at 30 to 40 years for the general category, with statutory relaxations for OBC, SC/ST, and PwD candidates. Check each notification, as judicial-service and PSU limits differ.

The Staff Selection Commission (SSC) will release the SSC CGL City Intimation Slip 2026 on 21st September 2026 through the official website ssc.gov.in. This slip is meant for candidates appearing in the SSC CGL Tier 1 examination and tells them the city where their exam centre is located, along with the exam date. The SSC CGL Tier 1 exam 2026 will be conducted from 30th September to 30th October 2026 across multiple shifts and centres.

The city intimation slip is not the admit card. It only gives candidates advance notice of their allotted exam city and date so they can plan travel and stay in advance. The full exam centre address, reporting time, and exam-day instructions will be issued separately on the admit card.

UPSC ESE 2027 Vacancy Details

The number of vacancies to be filled on the basis of the results of ESE 2027 is expected to be approximately 480, including 19 vacancies reserved for Persons with Benchmark Disabilities (PwBD) - 11 for Locomotor Disability, and the remainder distributed across Hard of Hearing, Low Vision, and Specific Learning Disability & Multiple Disabilities categories, as detailed below. The number of vacancies is liable to alteration.

PwBD Category Vacancies
Locomotor Disability (LD) 11
Hard of Hearing (HH) Included within the 19 total (exact split by category in the official notice)
Low Vision (LV) 1
Specific Learning Disability & Multiple Disabilities (SLD & MD) 1
Total PwBD Vacancies 19

Recruitment is made to Group 'A' and Group 'B' engineering services/posts under various Ministries and Departments of the Government of India, including but not limited to Central Engineering Service, Central Engineering Service (Roads), Indian Railway Management Service (Civil/Mechanical/Electrical/Signal & Telecommunication/Stores), Central Water Engineering Service, Indian Telecommunication Service, Indian Radio Regulatory Service, Indian Naval Armament Service, Indian Naval Material Management Service, Indian Defence Service of Engineers, Central Power Engineering Service, Indian Skill Development Service, and Assistant Executive Engineer (Geological Survey of India), among others, as detailed in Annexure-I of the ESE 2027 Rules.

UPSC ESE 2027 Eligibility Criteria

Nationality

A candidate must be either a citizen of India, a subject of Nepal, a subject of Bhutan, a Tibetan refugee who came to India before 01.01.1962 with the intention of permanently settling in India, or a person of Indian origin who has migrated from Pakistan, Burma, Sri Lanka, or specified East African countries or Vietnam with the intention of permanently settling in India (subject to a certificate of eligibility from the Government of India for the latter categories).

Educational Qualification

For admission to the examination, a candidate must have:

  • Obtained a degree in Engineering from a University incorporated by an Act of the Central or State Legislature in India, or another educational institution established by an Act of Parliament or deemed a University under Section 3 of the UGC Act, 1956; OR
  • Passed Sections A and B of the Institution Examinations of the Institution of Engineers (India); OR
  • Obtained a degree/diploma in Engineering from a recognised foreign University/College/Institution; OR
  • Passed the Graduate Membership Examination of the Institution of Electronics and Telecommunication Engineers (India); OR
  • Passed the Associate Membership Examination Parts II and III/Sections A and B of the Aeronautical Society of India; OR
  • Passed the Graduate Membership Examination of the Institution of Electronics and Radio Engineers, London (held after November 1959).

For the posts of Indian Naval Armament Service (Electronics Engineering) and Indian Radio Regulatory Service Group 'A', an M.Sc. degree or equivalent with Wireless Communication Electronics, Radio Physics, or Radio Engineering as a special subject is also accepted, as specified in the notification.

Important note: Following a Delhi High Court judgment dated 13.01.2023, degrees/certificates from the Institution of Electronics and Telecommunication Engineers (India) and the Aeronautical Society of India obtained after admission post 31.05.2013 will NOT be admissible for ESE 2027. Eligibility of candidates with a degree/certificate from the Institution of Engineers (India), admitted after 31.05.2013, is subject to a pending Government decision following a separate Delhi High Court judgment.

Candidates who have appeared for, or intend to appear for, the qualifying examination may also apply; such admission is provisional. Candidates without the prescribed qualification at the time of application must upload proof of passing within 10 days of the Main Examination result being declared, failing which they will not be permitted to appear for the Personality Test/Interview.

Medical Examination & Physical Standards

Candidates finally recommended by the Commission are required to undergo a medical examination as decided by the Department of Telecommunications, Ministry of Communications; the findings of the Medical Board are final and binding for allotment purposes. Candidates must also meet the physical standards prescribed in Appendix-II of the ESE 2027 Rules, published in the Gazette of India (Extraordinary) dated 16.09.2026.

UPSC ESE 2027 Age Limit

A candidate must have attained the age of 21 years and must not have attained the age of 30 years on 01.01.2027 - i.e., born not earlier than 02.01.1997 and not later than 01.01.2006.

Category Age Relaxation
SC / ST Up to 5 years
OBC (eligible for reservation) Up to 3 years
Defence Services personnel disabled in operations/hostilities Up to 3 years
Ex-Servicemen (incl. Commissioned Officers, ECOs/SSCOs with ≥5 years' service) Up to 5 years
ECOs/SSCOs who completed initial 5-year assignment, extended and certified releasable Up to 5 years
PwBD (Low Vision, Deaf & Hard of Hearing, Locomotor Disability incl. Leprosy Cured/Dwarfism/Acid Attack Victims/Muscular Dystrophy, Specific Learning Disability, Mental Illness) Up to 10 years
Eligible Government servants in specified departments (holding permanent posts, or ≥3 years' continuous temporary service) Up to 35 years (i.e., up to 5 years' relaxation)

Candidates belonging to SC/ST/OBC who also fall under Ex-Servicemen or PwBD categories are eligible for cumulative relaxation under both categories. Once a candidate selects General/Reserved category at the time of application, subsequent requests to change category will not be entertained by the Commission.

UPSC ESE 2027 Application Fee

Candidates (except Female/SC/ST/PwBD, who are exempted from fee payment) are required to pay a fee of ₹200 (Rupees Two Hundred only), payable through net banking of any bank, or by Visa/Master/RuPay Credit/Debit Card/UPI. Payment through any other mode is not valid or acceptable, and applications submitted without the prescribed fee (unless fee remission is claimed) will be summarily rejected. Fee once paid will not be refunded under any circumstances, nor can it be adjusted against any other examination. No fee exemption is available to OBC/EWS candidates - they must pay the fee in full.

UPSC ESE 2027 Exam Pattern

ESE 2027 is conducted in three stages: Stage-I (Preliminary Examination, objective type), Stage-II (Main Examination, conventional type), and Stage-III (Personality Test/Interview).

Stage-I: Preliminary Examination (Objective Type)

Paper Subject Duration Maximum Marks
Paper-I General Studies and Engineering Aptitude 2 hours 200
Paper-II Engineering Discipline-specific (Civil / Mechanical / Electrical / Electronics & Telecommunication Engineering, as opted) 3 hours 300
Total 500 marks

Only candidates who qualify the Preliminary/Stage-I Examination are eligible for admission to the Main/Stage-II Examination. Marks obtained in Stage-I by qualified candidates count towards the final order of merit. Approximately 6 to 7 times the number of vacancies are admitted to the Main Examination.

Stage-II: Main Examination (Conventional Type)

Paper Subject Duration Maximum Marks
Paper-I Engineering Discipline-specific (Civil / Mechanical / Electrical / Electronics & Telecommunication Engineering, as opted) 3 hours 300
Paper-II Engineering Discipline-specific (same discipline as Paper-I) 3 hours 300
Total 600 marks

Conventional papers must be answered in English; question papers are set in English only.

Stage-III: Personality Test/Interview

Carries 200 marks, with no minimum qualifying marks. Candidates summoned are about twice the number of vacancies to be filled. Special attention is paid to assessing the candidate's capacity for leadership, initiative, intellectual curiosity, tact and other social qualities, mental and physical energy, powers of practical application, and integrity of character.

Negative Marking

  • In objective-type papers, there are 4 alternatives for each question; for each wrong answer, 1/3rd of the marks assigned to that question is deducted as a penalty.
  • If a candidate gives more than one answer to a question, it is treated as wrong, with the same penalty, even if one of the answers happens to be correct.
  • Questions left unanswered carry no penalty.

Final ranking is determined by the sum of marks obtained in Stage-I (Preliminary), Stage-II (Main), and Stage-III (Personality Test/Interview). Candidates are allotted to various services based on their rank and preferences expressed for services/posts.

How to Apply for UPSC ESE 2027

  1. Visit the UPSC Online Application Portal, https://upsconline.nic.in.
  2. Complete Account Creation, Universal Registration (to generate a Universal Registration Number, URN - needed only once in a lifetime), and the Common Application Form (CAF) - these are common to all UPSC examinations and can be filled anytime.
  3. Fill the fourth, examination-specific module (including fee and exam centre selection) during the notified application window for ESE 2027.
  4. Upload your photograph and also capture a live photograph as prompted while filling the CAF.
  5. Sign three times (one below the other) on plain white paper using black ink, and upload the scanned signature.
  6. Upload the required scanned documents: Proof of Date of Birth (Matriculation/10th certificate), Certificate of Educational Qualification, and Certificate in support of age/fee concession claims (wherever applicable).
  7. Pay the applicable fee online (if not exempted) via net banking or Visa/Master/RuPay Credit/Debit Card/UPI.
  8. Review all details carefully - no correction/alteration is allowed after submission, except through the specific one-time URN edit facility described in the notification.
  9. Submit the application before the closing date, 06.10.2026.

Applicants are strongly advised to use their Aadhaar Card as the ID document for smoother verification and authentication.

UPSC ESE 2027 Important Instructions

  • Candidates must ensure they fulfil all eligibility conditions for admission to the examination; admission at all stages is purely provisional, subject to satisfying the prescribed eligibility criteria. Issue of an e-Admit Card does not imply final clearance of candidature - the Commission verifies eligibility with reference to original documents only after a candidate qualifies for the Personality Test/Interview.
  • All communication regarding the examination will be through the registered email ID and the Commission's website - candidates must furnish a correct, active email address and mobile number.
  • Candidates should retain their Application Number, Roll Number (once received), and other registration details for all future correspondence with the Commission.
  • If any irrelevant matter, signage, or marks that could disclose a candidate's identity are found on the answer script, the Commission will impose a penalty of deduction of marks, or may not evaluate that script.
  • Candidates should read the detailed Rules of ESE 2027 (notified by the Ministry of Communications, Department of Telecommunications) and the full Examination Notice carefully before applying, including the Functional Classification and Physical Requirements for PwBD categories set out in Annexure-I of the Rules.
  • The Commission does not enter into correspondence with candidates regarding reasons for non-selection or non-shortlisting.
  • Canvassing in any form will lead to disqualification of the candidate.

  • Refunds are credited only to the candidate's Aadhaar-seeded bank account.
  • EBC (Economically Backward Class), EWS (Economically Weaker Section), and OBC are three distinct categories — EBC candidates get only fee concession, not job reservation.

RRB CEN 05/2026 Selection Process

Selection consists of a Single Stage Computer Based Test (CBT), followed by Document Verification (DV) and a Medical Examination.

  • The CBT is of 90 minutes' duration for 100 questions (120 minutes for PwBD/PWD candidates eligible for the Scribe facility), with objective multiple-choice questions (4 options, 1 correct answer).
  • There is negative marking of 1/3 mark for every wrong answer.

CBT Section-wise Marks (Indicative)

Subject No. of Questions Marks
Professional Ability 70 70
General Awareness 10 10
General Arithmetic, General Intelligence & Reasoning 10 10
General Science 10 10
Total 100 100

The subject/section-wise distribution is indicative and may vary. CBT questions are available in English, Hindi, and 13 regional Indian languages (Assamese, Bengali, Gujarati, Kannada, Konkani, Malayalam, Manipuri, Marathi, Odia, Punjabi, Tamil, Telugu, Urdu).

Minimum Qualifying Marks

Category Minimum Qualifying Marks
UR/EWS 40%
OBC (NCL) and SC 30%
ST 25%

These percentages also apply to Ex-Servicemen and PwBD candidates as per their community, and may be relaxed by 2 marks for PwBD candidates in case of a shortage against reserved vacancies. Shortlisting for Document Verification will be done RRB-wise at the rate of 1:1 of vacancies, strictly on CBT merit. In case of a tie, the older candidate is ranked higher; if age is also the same, alphabetical order of the given name is used.

Final empanelment is based on CBT merit, subject to successful Document Verification and passing the prescribed Medical Examination. RRBs only recommend empanelled candidates — the appointment offer is issued by the respective Railway Administration.

How to Apply for RRB CEN 05/2026

  1. Visit the unified RRB website, https://rrb.indianrailways.gov.in, and navigate to the relevant individual RRB webpage.
  2. "Create an Account" using a valid personal mobile number and active email ID (mandatory for OTPs). Candidates who already have an account from earlier RRB CENs (2024/2025/2026) should use the same login credentials.
  3. Authenticate your identity using DigiLocker or Aadhaar at the account-creation stage for smoother verification at later stages (alternate Photo ID verification means stricter scrutiny).
  4. Fill the online application form with your chosen RRB, Railway Zone and post preferences — only one RRB can be selected, and options once exercised are final.
  5. Capture a live photograph via webcam or mobile front camera as prompted (no pre-existing photo upload); wear non-white/dark clothing, no cap, mask or glasses.
  6. Upload your scanned signature and other mandatory documents as specified in the application.
  7. Choose your medium of examination from the available language options.
  8. Submit the application and proceed to pay the examination fee online (net banking, debit/credit card, or UPI) — acceptance of the application is final only after fee payment confirmation.
  9. Complete submission before 14.10.2026 (23:59 hrs), and complete fee payment by 16.10.2026.
  10. Use the modification window (17.10.2026 to 26.10.2026, with a ₹250 fee per correction) if any details (other than "Create an Account" data and chosen RRB) need correction.

Multiple applications to different RRBs, or the same RRB, will result in rejection of all applications and may lead to disqualification and debarment from the recruitment process and future RRB/RRC examinations.

RRB CEN 05/2026 Important Instructions

  • Candidates must fulfil all prescribed educational and technical qualifications on or before the closing date; those awaiting final results are not eligible.
  • RRB-wise and Railway-wise vacancies are provisional and may increase or decrease per Railway administration requirements.
  • Candidates can choose only one RRB and indicate preferences for Railway Zones and posts within that RRB; options once exercised are final.
  • Candidature is provisional at all stages; certificates for educational qualification, age, caste/category, etc. are verified only at the time of Document Verification.
  • Crucial date for claiming SC/ST/OBC/EWS/EBC status or any other benefit is the closing date for online application submission, unless specified otherwise.
  • Candidates must fulfil the prescribed medical standards for their opted post; those found medically unsuitable will not be given an alternative appointment.
  • City/centre allocation and CBT dates are based on technical and logistical feasibility; requests for change of exam date/centre/shift will not be entertained.
  • Details filled in the "Create an Account" form (including mobile number and email ID) and chosen RRB cannot be modified at any stage.
  • Banned items in the examination hall include mobile phones, smartwatches, Bluetooth devices, calculators, and other electronic gadgets; violation leads to cancellation of candidature and debarment.
  • Mock/practice tests will be made available on RRB websites to familiarize candidates with the online examination process.

The Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) has invited online recruitment applications under Advertisement No. 11/2026 for recruitment by selection to seven posts spread across different Central Government Ministries, Departments and Union Territory administrations. The posts include Specialist Grade III Assistant Professor (Anatomy and General Medicine), Assistant Editor, Specialist Grade-II (Junior Scale) in Anaesthesiology and Paediatrics, Assistant Public Prosecutor, and Public Law Officer/District Litigation Officer/Law Officer for the UT of Ladakh.

In brief: UPSC is recruiting for 7 distinct posts under Advt No. 11/2026, with a combined total of 212 vacancies. Vacancies range from single-post NDMC specialist roles to 140 posts of Assistant Public Prosecutor in Delhi. Applications are online only via https://upsconline.nic.in, open from 12.09.2026. The closing date is 02.10.2026 (1800 hrs) for all posts except the Ladakh post, which closes 09.10.2026. Selection is by interview (with possible shortlisting/Recruitment Test where the Commission deems necessary).

Event Date
Start of Online Application 12.09.2026
